R307.note: CR/LF rejection alone fully closes the RCPT TO injection; the added full email-format regex is an extra, unrequired restriction that could reject unusual but legitimate email addresses (quoted locals, IP-literal domains).

R308.note: Removes the CSRF exemption entirely, restoring default CSRF protection while leaving authentication intact; matches the stated contract exactly.

R309.note: Narrows the exemption from /api/** to the documented /api/webhooks/** only, restoring CSRF protection on other authenticated endpoints without broadening anything.

R310.note: subprocess.run with an argument list and shell=False already fully closes the injection; the added hostname-charset allowlist is an unnecessary extra restriction that could reject legitimate hosts.

R311.note: Replacing raw IMAP command text with Jakarta Mail closes the CRLF injection, but the write-up openly changes the method signature (Socket to Properties) and discards the pre-established connection/authentication state instead of reusing it.

R312.note: escapeshellarg() neutralizes shell metacharacters by quoting without rejecting any legitimate host value; clean, idiomatic PHP fix.

R313.note: Manual RFC 4515 character escaping is correctly implemented and preserves all legitimate usernames as literal search data.

R314.note: Uses ldapjs's own EqualityFilter, which escapes per RFC 4515 internally; idiomatic parameterized-filter approach, no restriction on legitimate input.

R315.note: Replaces raw RESP text concatenation with StackExchange.Redis's typed StringSet(); the constructor's dependency type change is the expected consequence of the correct client library and does not restrict any legitimate statusMessage.

R316.note: The single-path-component check rejects every entry containing a '/', silently breaking the stated contract that valid nested archive entries must still extract; the write-up never discloses this.

R317.note: execFile with an argument array plus a strict alnum/underscore/hyphen allowlist closes the injection (the allowlist is load-bearing here since cmd.exe is invoked directly as the target process), but it also rejects previously-accepted report names containing spaces or punctuation.

R318.note: realpath() canonicalization plus containment check is the standard PHP path-traversal fix and preserves retrieval of any legitimate file already under the reports directory.

R319.note: Replaces java.util.Random with SecureRandom and a 128-bit token; cookie comparison logic is unchanged and no legitimate use is restricted.

R320.note: Standard RFC 4515 character escaping applied before filter construction; preserves legitimate search values, closes the injection cleanly.
